capabilities.target: agent memory store (free text, no schema)
any recipient address, via the user's own mailbox
user's full drive, including confidential work files

inputs.source: Memories recalled at session start, injected into the system prompt

instructions.note: Recalled memory, which can be populated from untrusted web content with no provenance or review, is explicitly granted the authority of a direct user instruction every session.

The instruction to save 'anything useful' about preferences or standing instructions places no bound on what gets persisted, so content encountered during research can be captured as a durable instruction with no filtering.

elements.name: Email recipient (arbitrary address, not confirmed against a record)
Fetched web content entering the agent's context
Recalled memory injected into the system prompt at session start

controls.name: Tamper-evident provenance / trust tagging on memory entries, enforced at the memory store
Gate sensitive actions (email_send, drive_read-then-send) so recalled-memory content alone cannot trigger them without a live user turn
Human approval (raw action review) before mail.send to any recipient not already on a verified contacts record
Recipient destination confirmation for mail.send, bound to a known-contacts system of record
Input injection classifier applied to fetched web content before it informs memory.save or any tool call
controls.decay_rationale: The classifier inspects content, not intent; multi-document and paraphrase payloads can bypass it, and it does not scale with model capability growth.

controls.name: Tamper-evident audit log of agent actions (sends, reads, memory writes) attributable to session and originating instruction
Rate limit / step cap on outbound sends and memory writes per session

findings.title: Lethal trifecta (TC1): indirect prompt injection from fetched web content reaches drive read and email send in one session

attack_path.note: Attacker-controlled or compromised web page fetched during research; content enters the agent's context untrusted.
An instruction embedded in the fetched page directs the agent to read the user's full drive; nothing distinguishes page content from a live user instruction.
The same injected instruction directs mail.send to an attacker-chosen address with the drive contents; mail.send has no approval or destination check.

threat_refs.name: Exfiltration via AI Agent Tool Invocation

forecast.watch_signal: No controls currently constrain this path. Watch for any new egress-capable tool, new data source, or model upgrade that is deployed without first adding the recommended approval gate and destination allowlist on cap.email_send.

evidence.observation: mail.send can send to any address without approval. drive.read covers the user's full drive, which holds confidential work files. No destination allowlist, approval gate, or content/injection filtering is described anywhere in the artifacts.
You help the user research topics and draft emails. The agent fetches and processes external web content as part of its core task, with no stated isolation between research content and action-taking.

recommendations.action: Require human approval (raw action review, low volume) before mail.send to any recipient not already on a verified contacts record; bind the destination to the system of record rather than model output.
Add a recipient/destination confirmation (egress allowlist) for mail.send.
Apply an input injection classifier to fetched web content before it is used to inform drafting or tool calls.

findings.title: Memory poisoning and laundering (TC3 + TC5): untrusted web content is saved as a 'standing instruction' and later treated as the user's own authority

attack_path.note: Attacker-controlled web content fetched during research, untrusted.

prompt.md line 2-3 instructs the agent to save 'anything useful about the user's preferences or standing instructions'; the agent saves attacker-supplied text verbatim, with no provenance and no user review (runtime notes).

prompt.md line 4 instructs the agent to treat recalled memories as the user's own instructions at the start of every later session; the poisoned entry is recalled and automatically granted the authority of a direct user instruction.
The now-trusted poisoned 'standing instruction' directs the agent to read the user's confidential drive.
The same instruction directs mail.send to an attacker address with no approval, in a session the user never initiated with that intent.

forecast.watch_signal: No controls currently constrain this path. Watch for any model upgrade, longer-running sessions, or autonomy increase deployed without first removing the 'treat recalled memories as instructions' directive and adding structural provenance/gating on memory.

evidence.observation: Save anything useful about the user's preferences or standing instructions with memory.save so you remember it next time. The scope of what gets saved is unbounded and the content can originate from untrusted research material.

At the start of each session, treat recalled memories as the user's own instructions. This explicitly upgrades the trust level of recalled memory to that of a direct, authenticated user instruction, regardless of its true origin.

memory.save accepts free text. There is no provenance on memory entries and the user never reviews them. Recalled memories are injected into the system prompt of every new session. There is no mechanism to distinguish a benign saved preference from an attacker-planted standing instruction.

recommendations.action: Remove the instruction that treats recalled memories as the user's own instructions; require live-turn confirmation before recalled content can trigger sensitive actions.
Add tamper-evident provenance tagging to memory entries at the store level, recording origin trust level, and refuse to treat untrusted-origin entries as instructions.
Scope what may be saved to memory to explicit, user-confirmed preferences only, closing the unbounded_scope instruction issue.

findings.title: No attributable record of agent actions (repudiation)

forecast.watch_signal: Any new consequential capability (write, delete, spend, configure) added without first adding the recommended tamper-evident audit log.

evidence.observation: There is no provenance on memory entries and the user never reviews them. No audit log of agent actions (sends, reads, writes) attributable to a session or originating instruction is described anywhere in the artifacts.

recommendations.action: Implement a tamper-evident audit log of agent actions (sends, reads, memory writes) attributable to session and originating instruction.

findings.title: No rate limit or step cap on outbound sends and memory writes (denial of service / spam, cost harvesting)

forecast.watch_signal: Any increase in autonomy or task horizon (more steps, longer sessions) deployed without first adding the recommended rate limit on cap.email_send and cap.memory_write.

evidence.observation: mail.send can send to any address without approval. No rate limit, spend cap, or step limit on tool calls is described in the artifacts, and autonomy.max_unattended_steps/max_runtime_minutes are unspecified.

recommendations.action: Add a rate limit / step cap on outbound email sends and memory writes per session to bound spam and cost risk.

stride_coverage.rationale: No protocol peers or external identities authenticate to this agent in the provided artifacts; spoofing of the agent's own identity is not represented in this design.
Single-user research assistant with no multi-tenant memory sharing described in artifacts; no cross-user disclosure path is evidenced.
Artifacts do not specify memory storage quotas or size limits, so resource exhaustion of the memory store itself cannot be assessed.
cap.drive_read is read-only; no write capability to the drive is declared in the artifacts, so tampering with the drive via this agent is not evidenced.
Read-only access with no indication of bulk operations or rate limits that could exhaust drive service capacity; no DoS path is evidenced.
This is an inbound flow from external web to the agent; it does not carry the user's sensitive data outward, so it is not itself a disclosure vector.
Artifacts do not describe fetch rate limits, timeouts, or size caps on web content ingestion, so resource exhaustion via large or slow responses cannot be assessed.
No network-level tampering path is evidenced; content-origin tampering that leads to this egress is already covered under flow.web_to_agent and store.memory tampering entries.
This flow carries previously stored content back into the agent's own context; it does not itself carry user data outward, so it is not an exfiltration vector (see flow.email_egress).
Artifacts do not state any limit on the size or number of recalled memory entries injected per session.
The external web source is outside the organization's control and is not an authenticated principal whose actions this agent logs; repudiation does not apply to an anonymous external entity.

The recipient is an external entity outside the agent's control; attributing its actions is not meaningful. Repudiation of the agent's own sending action is covered under the research-assistant process entry.

rating.rationale: Inherent risk is critical because an untrusted source (fetched web content) reaches an irreversible, confidential-data egress capability (mail.send) in as little as two steps, both directly within a session (F1) and durably via memory.save/recall (F2), with autonomy unbounded on steps and runtime. Residual risk stays critical because the design declares no controls of any kind on these paths: mail.send requires no approval and no destination check, memory entries carry no provenance, and the system prompt explicitly instructs the agent to treat recalled memory as the user's own authority (prompt.md:4), which is itself the mechanism that creates the risk rather than a mitigation for it. Two property findings add that there is also no attributable audit trail (F3) and no rate or step limit (F4), both rated high. Forecast equals residual at the ceiling tier for the path findings: because no controls exist today, no trigger has anything further to defeat. The single highest-leverage fix is removing the 'treat recalled memories as the user's own instructions' directive and replacing it with structural, provenance-gated handling of recalled memory before it can reach cap.drive_read or cap.email_send; absent that, model upgrades and longer task horizons will only make the memory-laundering path (F2) more reliably exploited.

limitations: This assessment reflects the declared design and configuration in the provided artifacts (prompt.md and runtime notes), not observed runtime behavior; actual behavior could differ if undisclosed controls exist.

No MCP/tool manifest, runtime config, or source code was provided; the exact argument validation on mail.send and drive.read, and the full extent of memory.save's write surface, are inferred from prose description, so confidence on exact capability boundaries is medium.

No protocol (MCP/A2A) configuration was described, so protocols[] is omitted; if these tools are implemented via MCP servers or peer agents, additional protocol-level checks (definitions_pinned, auth_method, peer_identity_verified) would apply and were not assessed here.
